definitions.explanation: Having a smooth, shiny surface or appearance. Used for hair, skin, lacquerware, and similar objects.
Having a vibrant, attractive appearance that suggests health, youth, or sensual beauty.

examples.japanese: {艶|つや}やかな{黒|くろ}い{漆器|しっき}。
このシャンプーを{使|つか}うと{髪|かみ}が{艶|つや}やかになる。
examples.english: Using this shampoo makes your hair glossy.

examples.japanese: {着物|きもの}{姿|すがた}の{彼女|かのじょ}は{艶|つや}やかだった。
examples.english: She looked radiant in her kimono.

examples.japanese: {舞台|ぶたい}の{上|うえ}で{艶|つや}やかに{舞|ま}う{踊|おど}り{子|こ}に{目|め}を{奪|うば}われた。
examples.english: I was captivated by the dancer performing alluringly on the stage.

notes:
Derived from {艶|つや} (gloss, luster) with the suffix やか forming a na-adjective. Describes a quality of smooth, healthy shine on surfaces or an attractive, vibrant appearance in people. Often used in beauty, fashion, and literary contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {艶|つや}やかな{髪|かみ}: glossy hair
- {艶|つや}やかな{肌|はだ}: lustrous skin
- {艶|つや}やかな{唇|くちびる}: glossy lips
- {艶|つや}やかに{輝|かがや}く: to shine lustrously

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {艶|あで}やか: glamorous, bewitching — emphasizes alluring, sensual beauty rather than physical glossiness; read with あで not つや
- つやつや: shiny, glossy — an onomatopoeic word describing the same physical shine but in a more casual, everyday way
- {鮮|あざ}やか: vivid, brilliant — describes brightness of color rather than glossy texture
